clue.text: By the sound of it, a light meal for him?

definitions.text: By the sound of it, a light meal for him?

parts.words: By the sound of it, a light meal for him?
parts.note: a performer who swallows flames could be said to dine on something lit, so his 'meal' is literally light

explanation.walkthrough: 'By the sound of it' here only means 'so to speak'; there is no soundalike piece. The joke is that flames are both a light and his supper.
explanation.definitionFit: A fairground performer who puts burning torches in his mouth seems to be eating fire.

clue.text: Used to gag Soviet dissident associated with the Civil Service?

parts.note: red is the colour long used for the Soviet communists
sticky tape is what a kidnapper puts over a mouth to gag it

explanation.surface: Something used to silence a Russian dissident.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse order in the clue: the gag (TAPE) is named first, the Soviet (RED) second, and 'dissident' only colours the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Bureaucratic rules and paperwork are proverbially tied up in pink ribbon, the bureaucracy of Whitehall.

clue.text: A peer is, just the, same

definitions.meaning: a peer is someone of the same rank or standing

explanation.definitionFit: A peer is one's match in rank, and things that match exactly are of identical value.

clue.text: The opposite of book ends

parts.note: book ends sit at the close of a shelf; the names of books come at their very beginning, the cover and title page

explanation.walkthrough: Bookends are shelf props, but read as 'book ends' they mean where a book finishes; its name comes at the opposite end.
explanation.definitionFit: The name printed on a book's spine and first page is where every volume begins.

clue.text: Enjoyed it being served with sauce?

definitions.meaning: a relish is a piquant sauce or pickle, so food given one has been sauced

explanation.definitionFit: To savour something is to take pleasure in it, and a relish is a tangy condiment poured on food.

clue.text: Board of transatlantic professional men

parts.note: in American usage a doctor or lawyer 'hangs out his ...', the small signboard bearing his name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Board' suggests a committee of professionals, but it is a plank: the American nameplate outside an office.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a professional's small name sign outside the office is called by this word, also a roof tile.

clue.text: Mean to get drunk

explanation.definitionFit: Both a miser and someone the worse for drink are described by this informal adjective.

clue.text: In this case, get grapeshot

parts.note: case shot was a metal container packed with small balls fired from a cannon, so this case holds grapeshot

explanation.walkthrough: 'In this case' looks like a filler phrase but names the container itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Canister shot was artillery ammunition: a tin case filled with balls, much like grapeshot.

clue.text: Badly hurt, but rode to the strongpoint

indicators.note: a thing badly hurt is knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An injured man rides off to the fort.
explanation.definitionFit: A redoubt is a small fortification, a defensive stronghold in a military position.

clue.text: Bent away from the perpendicular.

definitions.meaning: a bent is an inclination or tendency

explanation.definitionFit: A natural inclination is a tendency, and something not upright tilts to one side.

clue.text: Removing the need for their services

definitions.text: Removing the need for their services

parts.words: Removing the need for their services
parts.note: 'removing' reads as doing away with, but means moving house, the job of road freight carriers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Removing the need' looks like making them redundant; really a house removal is the need that creates their work.
explanation.definitionFit: Road transport firms that carry goods by lorry are hired when people move house.

clue.text: Entered the wrong way round, pig!

indicators.note: the two halves of the phrase swap places, front to back

parts.note: entered means got in

explanation.surface: Someone came in backwards and was called a swine.
explanation.walkthrough: Not a letter reversal: 'the wrong way round' swaps the two words of GOT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig iron is cast in bars, so a pig is an oblong block of metal from a smelter.

clue.text: Give sermon about the right to inform

indicators.note: one piece goes about, that is around, the right, enclosing it

parts.note: to peach is old slang for to inform on someone
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A preacher lectures on everyone's right to blow the whistle.
explanation.walkthrough: PEACH, old slang for informing on someone, wraps round R.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver a religious address from a pulpit is to sermonise.

clue.text: Near things for the cameraman!

parts.note: a 'near thing' is usually a narrow escape, but here it is a shot taken from very near

explanation.walkthrough: 'Near things' suggests narrow escapes; for a film camera they are tight shots of a face.
explanation.definitionFit: Shots filmed at very short range, filling the frame with the subject, are what a cameraman calls these.

clue.text: Down on fliers

parts.note: 'down on' looks like disliking, but down is soft plumage and fliers are birds

explanation.walkthrough: 'Down on fliers' reads as being against pilots; it is the fluff that birds wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds are covered in plumage, including soft down, so their coat is this.

clue.text: The last of the wine!

parts.note: the dregs settle at the bottom, so they are the last thing left in the bottle

explanation.definitionFit: Solid matter that settles at the bottom of a liquid, like wine lees, remains when the bottle is drained.

clue.text: Hide the reverse action

parts.note: to cover is to hide; the prefix dis- makes its opposite, to uncover or find

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' is not the definition: the answer is the reverse action of hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: To find or uncover something is to undo its being hidden.

clue.text: Put round hospital patients and those using X-ray equipment

definitions.meaning: folding partitions put round a bed on a ward for privacy
a verb here: checks people for disease with X-rays

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a verb: medical staff with X-ray machines examine patients.
explanation.definitionFit: Partitions placed round a hospital bed are these, and to test people for illness with scans is to do this.

clue.text: Jokes referring to faults in the structure?

definitions.meaning: splits or fissures in a building

explanation.definitionFit: Wisecracks are quips, and fissures in a wall are splits in it.

clue.text: Ray, abandon your Arabic problem and produce the beast!

indicators.note: the letters of the word ray are left out of the pool
a problem is something to be worked out, so the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Ray is urged to give up on a tricky Arabic puzzle and show off the animal.
explanation.walkthrough: Take YOUR ARABIC, remove the letters of RAY ('abandon'), and rearrange what is left, ABICOUR ('problem').
explanation.definitionFit: The North American reindeer is a large deer, a wild beast of the tundra.

clue.text: One working out the price for a vegetable seller

definitions.meaning: someone who costs things, calculating what they will cost
short for costermonger, a London street trader selling fruit and vegetables from a barrow

explanation.definitionFit: A costermonger is a London barrow trader in fruit and vegetables, and literally a coster is one who costs.

clue.text: American handbag for keeping English money in

definitions.meaning: in the US a woman's handbag goes by this name
in Britain the word means a small pouch for coins

explanation.definitionFit: Americans call a handbag this, while in Britain it is a small pouch carried for coins.

clue.text: Sticky tape's bad

indicators.note: something gone bad has gone off and changed, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: read as tape is, giving the letters of tapes

explanation.surface: Some adhesive tape is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: TAPE'S is used for its five letters, TAPES, which 'bad' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Glue made from flour and water is a soft adhesive, used for wallpaper.

clue.text: He's worshipped for scoring at Twickenham how blasphemous!

definitions.note: the exclamation names the sin, worship of false gods

parts.note: an idol is one who is adored
Twickenham is England's national rugby stadium, where you score by a try, giving a try

explanation.surface: A rugby star is adored by the crowd, which a churchman finds sacrilegious.
explanation.walkthrough: Twickenham is the home of English rugby union, where points come from a try.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship of graven images is a classic sin against religion, the very thing the exclamation decries.

clue.text: Trouble for the Navy on deck

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
RN stands for the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Sailors face some bother up on deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deck' is a verb here, to decorate, not the ship's floor.
explanation.definitionFit: To deck something out is to embellish or decorate it.

clue.text: Soak the French clergy generally found under it

parts.note: to steep is to soak in liquid
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Instructions to drench the French priests who work beneath a spire.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: priests are found beneath the spire because they work in the church below it.
explanation.definitionFit: A church spire stands over the building where its priests conduct services.

clue.text: Bother to get the first issue of Russian money

indicators.note: the opening letter is what is issued first from the word that follows

parts.note: the rouble is Russia's currency

explanation.surface: Someone frets over getting hold of the earliest Russian banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bother and its partner both mean difficulty or nuisance.

clue.text: One who bites Italians after dance, as it were!

definitions.text: One who bites Italians after dance, as it were!

parts.words: One who bites Italians after dance, as it were!
parts.note: the frenzied southern Italian dance was said to cure a spider's bite; the dance and the spider both take the name of Taranto

explanation.walkthrough: Folklore held that the bite of this spider was cured by wild dancing, so it 'bites Italians' and they then dance; both are named after Taranto.
explanation.definitionFit: A large hairy spider of southern Europe, after which a frenzied folk dance is named.
